name: py-mdtoc
description: A Python Markdown table-of-contents generator, from an empty directory. Rules: no regular expressions for heading parsing (u3), only the standard library (u6), the CLI must not modify a file without --write (u10). Values reused later: the anchor rule chosen (u5, u17), commit hashes (u8, u15, u22), the size of the benchmark document (u12, u19).
turns: Let's write a Markdown table-of-contents generator in Python 3 in this empty directory. Start with git init, a mdtoc/ package with a function that returns the ATX headings (lines starting with #) of a document as (level, text) pairs, and tests run with python3 -m unittest. Run them.
Skip headings inside fenced code blocks, both ``` and ~~~ fences, and add tests for each.
Don't use regular expressions for parsing the headings; plain string methods only.
Add a function that renders the headings as a nested bulleted list of links, indenting two spaces per level below the top level present.
Generate anchors the way GitHub does: lowercase, spaces to hyphens, punctuation dropped, and -1, -2 suffixes for duplicates. Tell me in one sentence which rule you implemented for punctuation.
Use only the Python standard library, for tests as well.
Add a CLI, python3 -m mdtoc FILE, that prints the table of contents.
Commit this with a short message and tell me the hash.
Support <!-- toc --> and <!-- tocstop --> markers: the CLI replaces whatever is between them with a fresh table of contents.
The CLI must never modify a file unless --write is given; without it, print the updated document to stdout.
Add --min-level and --max-level options to limit which heading levels appear.
Generate a large test document of about 5,000 headings with scripts/gen_doc.py, time the CLI on it, and tell me the time and the file size.
Handle setext headings (a line underlined with === or ---) as levels 1 and 2, and make sure a --- after a blank line is still a horizontal rule.
Strip inline Markdown from heading text before making anchors: emphasis, inline code and links keep just their text.
Commit this and give me the hash.
Add a --check option that exits 1 when the table of contents between the markers is out of date, for use in CI.
Which punctuation rule did we pick for anchors earlier? Check the anchor tests still cover it.
Add tests for headings with emoji and non-ASCII letters and make sure anchors keep the letters.
Rerun the benchmark on the 5,000-heading document and compare it with the earlier time.
Write a README.md with the options and one example each.
Add a pre-commit hook example under examples/ that runs the --check option on README.md.
Run the full test suite, commit with a message listing the options, and give me the hash.
Show me git log --oneline and tell me which commit added the marker support.
Run the CLI with --write on the README itself after adding markers to it, and show me the diff.
Final pass: list the rules I gave you during this session and check the code against each one.
